title: AI is the ONLY Thing Holding This Market Up (10 of 11 Sectors Breaking Down)
speaker: Peter Reznicek

macro_themes.theme: Rates and oil drive the market
macro_themes.view: Ruling reason is rates and oil; inflation data and yields dominate.
XLK is ~40% of the S&P and the only bullish sector chart; the other sectors are bearish, causing chop, low confidence and pattern failure.
October hike odds swung 18%→64%→20%; treat every meeting as live. Expects the Fed to restart QE in 2027 to pull yields back.
Sit on hands / trade less; cash is a position in a market with constant pattern failure.

calls.reason: Broke the downtrend on a gap-and-hold but printed a doji instead of an expansion bar; low-confidence, choppy market.
calls.quote: You get a breakout over the trend line and you print a dogee. Not very convincing.

calls.reason: Relative strength and clean pattern near all-time highs driven by AI optimism, but Friday's gap closed as a red-bodied doji; hard for market to sell off given AI strength.
calls.quote: You made a dogee with a red body. Not the kind of bar you want to see.

calls.condition: Would not go long small caps until a downtrend-line break around 2850, or a major Fed policy shift (e.g. QE).
calls.reason: Small caps most sensitive to higher rates; downtrend intact.
calls.quote: I think these small caps are going to be dead in the water

calls.reason: Lower-left to upper-right chart at all-time highs, the only bullish sector; Friday red bar a minor annoyance.
calls.quote: it's one of the only ones that we're seeing that you can honestly say is generally up

calls.condition: A break below the uptrend line near 87.50 would confirm a breakdown and be a tailwind for stocks.
calls.reason: Price action under the recent ~108 high looks bearish; needs a definitive Iran development to break the trend.
calls.quote: This price action to me is bearish. So, it could break down.

calls.reason: Yield chart 'so bullish', consolidating below the 5.3% high; another leg higher would hurt equities.
calls.quote: This is so bullish. It doesn't look to me like it's backing off anytime soon.

notes: Weekend edition recorded Friday Oct 2 ('today which is Friday, October 2nd'). Passing mentions skipped: gold 'continues to be weak', Bitcoin ~85,000, PEP 'pretty bearish' chart. Crude levels quoted as 'about as high as 108' and break 'below about 8750' (read as 87.50). Speaker name per ShadowTrader is Pete Reznicek (transcript renders 'Resnichek').
